Pathways

Pathways by goal

Pick the sequence that matches what you want to do. Each pathway names the levels and the lessons that serve it.

Start with Level 1

Start here: new to architecture

Developers and analysts who build software but have never been asked to design it. Open the free lessons first, then take the design and documentation lessons in order.

Levels: Level 1

  • L1What Software Architecture Is and What Architects DoFree
  • L1Stakeholders, Requirements and Constraints
  • L1Quality Attributes and Measurable Scenarios
  • L1Design Approaches and Decomposition
  • L1Documenting and Communicating ArchitectureFree
  • L1Worked Example: The Integrated Case Study

Prepare for the iSAQB Foundation exam

Learners who plan to sit the external iSAQB CPSA-F exam. Lessons 1 to 12, then the exam-strategy lesson and the mock exams. Lesson 13 (AI) is optional extra for now. Check the exam rules with a certification body.

Levels: Level 1

  • L1What Software Architecture Is and What Architects DoFree
  • L1Stakeholders, Requirements and Constraints
  • L1Quality Attributes and Measurable Scenarios
  • L1Design Approaches and Decomposition
  • L1Design Principles and Patterns
  • L1Interfaces, Contracts and Data Models
  • L1Runtime Views and Distributed Systems
  • L1Deployment and Infrastructure
  • L1Cross-Cutting Concepts
  • L1Documenting and Communicating ArchitectureFree
  • L1Analysing and Assessing Architecture
  • L1Worked Example: The Integrated Case Study
  • L1Exam Strategy and the Final Mock

Document a system well

Engineers and tech leads who must leave a system understandable to the next team. The Level 1 documentation lesson, then arc42 section by section.

Levels: Level 1, Level 2

  • L1Documenting and Communicating ArchitectureFree
  • L2Section 1: Introduction and goals
  • L2Section 2: Constraints
  • L2Section 3: Context and scope
  • L2Section 4: Solution strategy
  • L2Section 5: Building blocks
  • L2Section 6: Runtime view
  • L2Section 7: Deployment view
  • L2Section 9: Architecture decisions
  • L2Section 10: Quality requirements
  • L2Sections 11 and 12: Risks and glossary

Decide and defend

Architects and senior engineers who choose between designs and must justify the choice. Numbers first, then options, then the written decision.

Levels: Level 2, Level 3

  • L3Quality Models and the Quality TreeFree
  • L3Writing Quality Scenarios
  • L3When Qualities Conflict
  • L3Options, Criteria and Trade-off Analysis
  • L3Architecture Decision Records in PracticeFree
  • L3Reversible and Irreversible Decisions
  • L3Scenario-Based Design Review

Design with AI agents

Teams that use coding agents or put agents into the product. Verification and provenance first, then the Level 4 agent-design course. For the security side, see the Cybersecurity Academy.

Levels: Level 1, Level 3, Level 4

  • L1AI-Assisted Architecture Work
  • L2Agents as readers of your documentation
  • L3Using LLMs to Draft Options and Records
  • L3Decisions Your Coding Agents Can Follow
  • L4Workflows, assistants and agents: choosing the shapeFree
  • L4The agentic loop and tools as contracts
  • L4Levels of autonomy and the human in the loop
  • L4Architecture knowledge agents can read: decision records, rules and specificationsFree
  • L4A harness of preventive and detective controls
  • L4Architecture tests and drift checks in the pipeline

Lead architecture

Senior architects and heads of engineering. Levels 5 and 6 are planned. This path shows what to take today and where it leads.

Levels: Level 3, Level 5, Level 6

  • L3Architecture Decision Records in PracticeFree
  • L3Fitness Functions and Architecture Drift
  • L3Risk Storming
  • L4Keeping judgment: ownership, skill and the architect’s changing role

Reviewed 2026-11-25. Intellica is independent of iSAQB, arc42, ISO, IEC, IEEE and the Software Engineering Institute. Mappings show how our lessons relate to published topics. They are not an affiliation, an approval or a prediction of any exam result.
